name_en: Sweet Potato Stem Stir-simmer — the leaf-stalk of the vine, cooked crisp-tender in dashi
summary_ja: さつまいもの茎（葉柄）を炒めてから出汁で甘辛く煮る高知の常備菜。高温多湿な気候で茂る茎を活かした農家の知恵とされ、彩りに唐辛子を添え、揚げ物を加えてアレンジすることも多いという。
summary_en: The leaf-stalk of the sweet potato vine is stir-fried, then simmered sweet and salty in dashi — a Kochi staple side dish. Said to have grown from farm households making use of stems that thrive in the hot, humid climate, it's often finished with red chili and sometimes bulked out with fried fish cake.
source_title: いもの茎の炒め煮 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Guruni — a big-batch winter simmer of daikon, taro, and whatever root vegetable was on hand
summary_ja: 大根や人参、里芋などの根菜を出汁じゃこと醤油で煮込む冬の総菜。土佐弁で「仲間」を意味する「ぐる」が名の由来とされ、何度も温め直しながら食べる備蓄菜として親しまれてきたという。
summary_en: Daikon, carrot, taro, and other root vegetables are simmered together in a dashi made from dried baby sardines and soy sauce — a winter side dish. The name is said to come from "guru," Tosa dialect for a group of companions, and the dish was long made in bulk and reheated meal after meal.
source_title: ぐる煮 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_ja: りゅうきゅうの酢の物
name_en: Ryukyu no Sunomono — the crisp leaf-stalk of taro-leaf vine, dressed in yuzu vinegar with hairtail
summary_ja: ハスイモの葉柄「りゅうきゅう」を塩もみし、柚子酢に浸したタチウオなどの魚としょうが、ごまで和える高知の夏の定番。名は沖縄伝来の説があるが定かではないとされ、地域で使う魚が違うという。
summary_en: The crisp leaf-stalk of the taro-leaf vine, known locally as ryukyu, is salted and tossed with hairtail or another fish that's been steeped in yuzu vinegar, ginger, and sesame — a summer standard in Kochi. One theory traces the name to Okinawa, though it's said to be unconfirmed, and the fish used varies by area.
source_title: りゅうきゅうの酢の物 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Itadori no Aburaitame — a tart, crunchy mountain shoot, salted or frozen for year-round eating
summary_ja: 山あいに自生するタデ科の若芽「いたどり」の皮をむき、湯通しして酸味を抜いてから油で炒め、醤油と砂糖で味付ける。春にしか採れないため塩漬けや冷凍で保存し、通年食卓にのぼるという。
summary_en: The young shoots of itadori, a mountain-growing knotweed, are peeled, blanched to draw out their tartness, then stir-fried in oil and seasoned with soy sauce and sugar. Since the shoots appear only in spring, they're salted or frozen for storage and eaten from the pantry year-round.
source_title: いたどりの油いため 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_ja: ひめいちとみかんの辛子煮
name_en: Himeichi to Mikan no Karashini — a small sea-bream stand-in simmered with citrus peel and hot mustard
summary_ja: 土佐湾でとれる小魚ヒメイチを、種を抜いた辛子とみかんの皮とともに弱火でじっくり煮る。安価にタイの代役を果たしたとされ、骨まで柔らかくなるため年の暮れに大量につくり保存食にしたという。
summary_en: Himeichi, a small fish caught in Tosa Bay, is simmered slowly over low heat with seeded hot mustard and citrus peel. Prized as an affordable stand-in for sea bream, the long simmer softens even the bones, and it was traditionally made in bulk at year's end to keep through the season.
source_title: ひめいちとみかんの辛子煮 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kure no Nimono — whale meat simmered with daikon and kelp for New Year's Eve
summary_ja: くじら肉を大根や人参、こんにゃく、糸昆布と煮込む高知の年越し料理。大きなものを食べて「大物になるように」との願いが込められたとされ、捕鯨の町として知られる室戸市がその文化を担ってきた。
summary_en: Whale meat is simmered with daikon, carrot, konjac, and shredded kelp — a New Year's Eve dish in Kochi. Eating something so large is said to carry a wish for one's children to grow into something big themselves, and the whaling town of Muroto has long carried the tradition.
source_title: 暮れの煮物 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Taimo no Korobashi — taro rolled in sesame after a long, slow soy-sugar simmer
summary_ja: 里芋を高知では田芋と呼び、醤油と砂糖でじっくり煮詰めてから炒りごまをまぶす佐川町の郷土料理。ごまの上で芋を転がすことが名の由来とされ、子孫繁栄の縁起物として皿鉢料理にも加わるという。
summary_en: Taro, called taimo in Kochi, is slowly simmered down in soy sauce and sugar, then rolled in roasted sesame — a dish from Sakawa Town. The name is said to come from rolling the taro over the sesame, and as a symbol of a family's growing lineage, it also appears on festive sawachi platters.
source_title: 田芋のころばし 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_ja: 淡竹とエンドウの煮物
name_en: Hachiku to Endo no Nimono — slender purple-skinned bamboo shoot simmered with fresh peas
summary_ja: 身が薄く淡白な淡竹（はちく）を出汁で煮て、実をつけ始めたエンドウを加えて仕上げる高知の初夏の煮物。孟宗竹に続いて出回る淡竹と、同じ頃に収穫期を迎えるエンドウの組み合わせという。
summary_en: Hachiku, a slender, purple-tinged bamboo shoot with a mild flavor, is simmered in dashi and finished with fresh green peas just coming into season — an early-summer simmered dish in Kochi. It pairs hachiku, which follows the earlier moso bamboo to market, with peas harvested around the same time.
source_title: 淡竹とエンドウの煮物 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Sawachi Ryori — a single vast platter piled with sushi, sashimi, and simmered dishes for a party
summary_ja: 36〜39cmほどの大皿に刺身やかつおのたたき、すし、煮物、揚げ物などを盛り合わせる高知の宴会様式。「おきゃく」と呼ぶ客をもてなす場で振る舞われ、皿の枚数で宴の規模がわかるとされる。
summary_en: Sashimi, seared bonito, sushi, simmered dishes, and fried food are piled onto a single platter roughly 36 to 39 centimeters across — a style of feasting in Kochi. Served at gatherings called okyaku, the number of platters set out is said to signal the scale of the party.
source_title: 皿鉢料理 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Chate no Aemono — chayote, sliced raw and tossed while still crisp
summary_ja: 熱帯アメリカ原産のウリ科植物チャーテ（ハヤトウリ）を生のまま和え物にする高知の秋の家庭料理。1株で100個以上実るため自家消費や近所への差し入れに使われ、栽培しやすい山間部で特に親しまれている。
summary_en: Chayote, a squash-family vine native to tropical America and known locally as chate, is tossed raw into a light dressing — an autumn home dish in Kochi. A single vine can bear over a hundred fruit, so it's mostly grown for the household or shared with neighbors, and it's especially popular in the mountains where it grows easily.
source_title: チャーテの和え物 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Zenmai no Itameni — mountain fern, dried and re-hydrated, stir-simmered with fried tofu
summary_ja: ゆでて天日干しを何度も繰り返した乾燥ぜんまいを戻し、油揚げと炒め煮にする大豊町の郷土料理。繰り返しの乾燥で繊維が柔らかくなるとされ、皿鉢料理の一品としてもよく登場するという。
summary_en: Zenmai fern, repeatedly boiled and sun-dried until fully cured, is re-hydrated and stir-simmered with fried tofu — a dish from Otoyo Town, known for its zenmai. The repeated drying is said to soften the fern's fiber, and the dish is a regular on sawachi platters.
source_title: ぜんまいの炒め煮 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_ja: きゅうりと川エビの煮物
name_en: Kyuri to Kawaebi no Nimono — river prawns simmered with cucumber until glossy with starch
summary_ja: 四万十川などでとれる川エビ（テナガエビ）と地這きゅうりを出汁で煮て、水溶き片栗粉でとろみをつける高知の夏の一皿。柴を束ねた仕掛けで獲る伝統漁法が今も伝わり、子どもの川遊びの成果だったという。
summary_en: River prawns caught in rivers like the Shimanto and a local trailing cucumber are simmered in dashi and thickened with a cornstarch slurry — a summer dish in Kochi. A traditional method using bundled brushwood traps is still used to catch the prawns, once the reward of a child's day playing in the river.
source_title: きゅうりと川エビの煮物 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_ja: きびなごのほおかぶり
name_en: Kibinago no Hokaburi — vinegared kibinago fish wrapped around a ball of seasoned tofu pulp
summary_ja: 背開きにして酢でしめたキビナゴで、酢で味付けて炒ったおからを丸めた玉を包む「たまずし」の一種。すしの形が頬かむりした人の頭に見えることが名の由来とされ、宿毛市が特産品としてPRしている。
summary_en: Small kibinago fish are butterflied, cured in vinegar, and wrapped around a ball of tofu pulp that's been pan-toasted and seasoned with vinegar — a variant of tamazushi, sushi made with pulp instead of rice. The wrapped shape is said to resemble a head wrapped in a cloth, and Sukumo City promotes it as a local specialty.
source_title: きびなごのほおかぶり 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kashikiri — acorn flour, leached of bitterness for two days, set into a tofu-like block
summary_ja: かしの実（どんぐり）を粉砕し、水を何度も替えて2日ほどかけて渋抜きしてから練り上げる豆腐状の食品。飢饉の際の救荒食として山間部で広く食べられたが、今では安芸市南部でのみ伝わる貴重な料理という。
summary_en: Acorns are ground, then leached of bitterness over some two days of repeated water changes, and worked into a tofu-like block. Once widely eaten across the mountains as emergency food in lean years, it survives today only in southern Aki City, where it's treated as a rare local dish.
source_title: かしきり 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Mushidai — a whole sea bream stuffed with seasoned tofu pulp and steamed
summary_ja: タイの腹に味付けしたおからや人参、しいたけ、卵などを詰めて丸ごと蒸す高知の祝い料理。「おきゃく」と呼ばれる宴席に欠かせない一皿とされ、かつてはどの家にも専用のセイロがあったという。
summary_en: A whole sea bream is stuffed with seasoned tofu pulp, carrot, shiitake, and egg, then steamed whole — a celebratory dish in Kochi. Considered essential to the feasts called okyaku, it's said every household once kept its own steamer just for this dish.
source_title: 蒸し鯛 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_ja: ねぎとさつまいものぬた
name_en: Negi to Satsumaimo no Nuta — leek and sweet potato dressed in sweet vinegar miso
summary_ja: ゆでたねぎとさつまいもを白味噌ベースの酢味噌で和える南国市の一皿。定番の「ねぎといかのぬた」のイカをさつまいもに置き換えたとされ、地場産品を生かした料理研究から生まれたという。
summary_en: Boiled leek and sweet potato are tossed in a white-miso-based sweet vinegar dressing — a dish from Nankoku City. Said to swap in sweet potato for the squid used in the more common negi-to-ika no nuta, it grew out of local research into using homegrown produce.
source_title: ねぎとさつまいものぬた 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Ha Ninniku no Nuta — a vinegar-miso dressing of ground garlic greens, poured over raw fish
summary_ja: 刻んですり潰した葉にんにくに味噌や酢、ごま、砂糖を混ぜる高知の伝統的な調味料。朝鮮渡来が由来と伝わり、ブリなど生の魚に醤油の代わりにかけるのが一般的で、地域ごとに呼び名や具材が違うという。
summary_en: Garlic greens are chopped, ground, and mixed with miso, vinegar, sesame, and sugar — a traditional Kochi condiment said to trace back to a Korean import. It's commonly spooned over raw fish like yellowtail in place of soy sauce, and both its name and the fish it accompanies vary by area.
source_title: 葉にんにくのぬた 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
